slides.title: Truths [[1–4]]

carousels.name: It's in the WHO's ICD-11. Stop calling it just a habit.

slides.title: Compulsive p*rn use is in the WHO's diagnostic manual. [[Stop calling it "just a habit."]]
slides.sub: Calling it small is how it stays big.

slides.title: It's [[official]]
slides.body: Since 2019, the World Health Organization's ICD-11 includes compulsive sexual behaviour disorder — and compulsive p*rn use is one of the ways it shows up.

slides.title: Of adults [[screened positive]]
slides.body: A JAMA Network Open study (2018) of 2,325 U.S. adults found 8.6% screened positive for compulsive sexual behavior. That's nearly 1 in 12.

slides.title: "Just a habit" is a [[lie]]
slides.body: You don't lie about a habit. You don't hide a habit. You don't fail to quit a habit 10 times. Be honest about what p*rn has become.

slides.title: Treat it [[seriously]]
items: Talk to a professional if it's severe.

carousels.name: The 20 minutes of a p*rn urge, minute by minute

slides.kicker: Save this for the next urge
slides.title: What happens in the 20 minutes of a [[p*rn urge]] — minute by minute.
slides.sub: If you know the shape of the wave, you can ride it.

slides.title: The [[spark]]
slides.body: A trigger hits — boredom, a photo, a feeling. The p*rn urge feels sudden and urgent. This is the moment to move, not think.

slides.title: The [[peak]]
slides.body: Your brain starts bargaining: "just a quick look." The p*rn urge feels strongest here. Get up and leave the room.

slides.title: The [[fade]]
slides.body: If you don't feed it, the urge usually starts to drop. Move, breathe, talk to someone. Watch it shrink.

slides.title: The [[win]]
slides.body: Most urges pass within minutes when you don't act on them. Every wave you ride out teaches your brain p*rn isn't the answer.
slides.note: Save this and check the clock next time a p*rn urge hits 🔖

carousels.name: What to say to a friend who relapsed on p*rn

slides.title: Your friend just relapsed on p*rn. [[Here's what to say.]]
Don't [[say]]
slides.body: "Bro, it's not a big deal." "You'll never quit lol." "Just use more willpower." Jokes and lectures push people back to p*rn.

slides.title: Do [[say]]
slides.body:
"Thanks for telling me."
"One slip doesn't erase your progress."
"What happened before it — and what can help next time?"

slides.title: Then [[show up]]
slides.body: Check in the next day. Invite them out. Offer to be their accountability partner for quitting p*rn. Presence beats advice.

slides.title: Be the [[friend]]
slides.note: Tag the friend who'd say the right thing ↗
